items.title: Epsilon from the filtered knot Floer complex

items.axiom_use: The finite algebraic definition uses no choice. The full-AC edge is retained from the controlling KT-42 interface; the actual analytic grid supplier uses ACω, a separate branch.
items.statement:
Work over $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ chain complex with Maslov grading $M$ and bifiltration coordinates $(i,j)$. Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. Define
$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

items.axiom_use: The finite Maslov-zero minimax uses no choice. The full-AC edge is retained from KT-42; the in-run analytic grid supplier states ACω, which is not being upgraded to full AC.
items.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot smoothly concordant to the unknot. Then there are finite-rank free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ bifiltered chain complexes $A$ and $B$, each having zero total homology, such that
$$ \mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A\simeq \Lambda\oplus B, $$
where $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ is the normalized unknot complex with zero differential and generator in Maslov grading and both filtration coordinates zero, and $\simeq$ is a Maslov-graded filtered chain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies do not increase either filtration. The acyclic summands are acyclic only after the filtrations are forgotten; no acyclicity of their associated-graded complexes is asserted.

items.axiom_use: Only finite-dimensional basis changes are made; no choice axiom is used.
items.statement: Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be the finite-rank free $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ knot Floer complex of a smooth oriented knot, with its Maslov grading, algebraic filtration $i$, Alexander filtration $j$, and weighted filtration $F_t=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j$ for a fixed $t\in[0,2]$. Assume its total homology is $\Lambda$ generated in Maslov grading zero. Then the filtered graded complex $(C,F_t)$ admits a filtered direct-sum decomposition $C=T\oplus A$, where $T=\Lambda\alpha$, $\partial\alpha=0$, $\alpha$ represents the normalized homology generator at filtration $\nu_t(C)$, and $A$ is acyclic as a graded complex. In the t-modified complex, the non-torsion tower from $T$ has maximal grading $-2\nu_t(C)$; hence this maximum equals the cycle-minimax definition of $\Upsilon_K(t)$.

items.axiom_use: The quotient and t-modification are finite algebraic constructions and use no choice. The full-AC edge is retained from KT-42; the grid analytic branch uses the separately declared ACω assumption.
items.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n\times n$ toroidal grid diagram representing a knot. Let $GC^-(G)$ be the finite grid complex over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$ with its Maslov grading $M$ and Alexander filtration $A$. Form the diagonal quotient
$$ D_G=GC^-(G)/(U_1-U_2,\ldots,U_1-U_n), $$
regarded as a finitely generated $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex with $U=U_1=\cdots=U_n$.

For a finitely generated Maslov-graded, Alexander-filtered complex $D$ over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with a fixed finite homogeneous basis, its $t$-modified complex for $t\in[0,2]$ is the free $\mathcal R$-module on that basis, where $\mathcal R$ is the ring of formal $\mathbb F_2$-series $\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ with support $A\subset[0,\infty)$ such that every nonempty subset of $A$ has a least element. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $\operatorname{gr}_t(x)=M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$; this action lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. The formula $M-tA$ is specified on the chosen polynomial generators. On Laurent translates, the extended grading is $M-t(j-i)$, with $v$ lowering both filtration coordinates by $1/2$. If
$$ \partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y, $$
then the modified differential is
$$ \partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y. $$
A homogeneous homology class is **non-torsion** if no nonzero element of $\mathcal R$ annihilates it. For $0\le t\le1$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ to be the maximum $t$-grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D_G^t)$. For $1<t\le2$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$. This is the grid convention compared with the original cycle-minimax invariant.

items.axiom_use: The finite filtered threshold argument and the least-integer definition use no choice. The planned analytic cobordism branch uses ACω as declared by its suppliers; full AC is not inferred or used.
items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ have a finite homogeneous basis $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ with Maslov grading $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any $\mathbb Z$-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$ that is finitely generated as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module, with $U$ of Maslov degree $-2$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

items.axiom_use: The finite hook, tensor, grid-rank and staircase arguments are choice-free. Actual normalized knot models and geometric comparisons reuse the supplied countable-choice interfaces; the approved separate full-AC dependency is retained.
items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $G$ be any $n\times n$ grid diagram representing a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Form the diagonal grid complex by setting every marking variable $U_i$ equal to a single variable $U$, and define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ by the t-modified non-torsion grading on that complex for $0\le t\le1$, extended by $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$ for $1<t\le2$. Then for every $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $\Upsilon_K$ is the finite cycle-minimax invariant defined from $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$. In this statement the quotient with all $U_i$ identified carries the factor $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$, where $W$ has generators in Maslov/Alexander bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$; this factor is retained in the proof and is not counted as an improvement to the grid-state complexity bound.

references.title: Peter S. Ozsvath, Andras I. Stipsicz, and Zoltan Szabo, Concordance homomorphisms from knot Floer homology, §§2–5

items.axiom_use: The finite cycle-minimax argument uses no choice. The cobordism-map route in the four-ball bound uses the ACω analytic branch. The full-AC plan edge is retained separately and is not treated as implied by ACω.
items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ be the smooth knot concordance group, with addition induced by oriented connected sum and inverse represented by reverse mirror. The function $\epsilon: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\to\{-1,0,1\}$ is well-defined and concordance-invariant, but it is not a homomorphism to $\mathbb Z$. The map
$$ \Upsilon:\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R),\qquad [K]\longmapsto\Upsilon_K, $$
is a group homomorphism, where $\mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R)$ is the abelian group of continuous piecewise-linear real-valued functions under pointwise addition. For every representative $K$ and $0\le t\le1$, its value satisfies $|\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$.

items.statement: Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ be the right-handed trefoil staircase on generators $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. The claim that $\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(1)$ is obtained by minimizing $F_1(x)$ over the individual displayed basis terms $x_0,x_1,x_2$, instead of over Maslov-zero cycles representing the normalized generator, is false. Assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized grid/analytic comparison, under the diagonal-grid convention every grid diagram of the trefoil also has grid Upsilon value $-1$ at $t=1$.

items.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $T_{2,3}$ be the right-handed trefoil and $-T_{2,3}$ its reverse mirror. A filtered basis for $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ is $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. Under the conventions of this page,
$$ \epsilon(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=\begin{cases}-t,&0\le t\le1,\\ t-2,&1\le t\le2.\end{cases} $$
The graph has its unique interior breakpoint at $t=1$. For the reverse mirror, $\epsilon(-T_{2,3})=-1$ and $\Upsilon_{-T_{2,3}}(t)=-\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)$.
